		&& (a \times b) \times c & = a \times (b\times c)\\
		\emph{Commutativity}&&a + b &= b+ a  \\
		&&  a \times b&= b\times a\\ 
		\emph{Identities}&&a + 0 &= a \\

changes.sense: Two bijective functions f:A→B and g:B→C used to prove transitivity of equinumerosity by composition.
changes.rationale: Retain the token-rendered plural «دوال تقابلية». The sentence explicitly supplies two functions and then composes them; the plural noun and feminine adjective thus represent bijections as bijective functions. The Damascus Academy page 69 gives «تقابل» for bijection and «تطبيق تقابلي» for bijective mapping. The current phrase uses the same attested تقابل family while adapting the noun to the edition's دالة terminology and to the plural context.

inverse $f^{-1}$ exists and is also !!{bijective}. Hence,
$f^{-1}\colon B \to A$ is !!a{bijection}, so $\cardeq{B}{A}$.

\emph{Transitivity.} Suppose that $\cardeq{A}{B}$ and $\cardeq{B}{C}$,
i.e., there are !!{bijection}s $f\colon A \to B$ and $g\colon B \to
C$. Then the composition $\comp{f}{g}\colon A \to C$ is !!{bijective},
so that $\cardeq{A}{C}$.
\end{proof}
